1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.Bd.strategy: Reinforces d4 with a pawn, the only good way to hold it. White cannot give up the centre: if the d-pawn takes on c5, the pawn on e5 loses its support and falls to the knight. The chain is stable and White has the space, while Black has to keep working against it.

Adds a second attacker on d4, which only the c-pawn defends, so White must reinforce it with a piece or give it up for development. This is the main line: Black develops and increases the pressure at the base of White's chain.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.Bd.name: French Defence: Tarrasch Variation, Closed Variation

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.Bd.strategy: Prepares to trade Black's bad light-squared bishop for White's good one, and adds a pawn defender to c5. It deals with the structure's main strategic problem, at the cost of a slower attack on d4, so White gets time to organise the defence.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.Bd.name: French Defence: Tarrasch Variation, Botvinnik Variation
